raw_text:
Below is a complete, integrated 12‑week program tailored for your 36‑year‑old recreational lifter returning from a right medial meniscus tear (surgeon cleared for low‑impact strength only — NO jumping and NO deep knee flexion under load). It combines strength (progressive phases), challenging low‑impact cardio (twice/week), nutrition to maintain weight, and recovery/mobility. The plan is structured week‑by‑week with clear session templates, progression rules, recovery recommendations and testing/peaking details so he feels strong by Week 12. Adjust loads based on his RPE and knee symptoms; if anything creates sharp pain or swelling increase >2/10, regress and consult physio/surgeon.

Quick summary of structure
- Frequency: Strength 3–4×/week (phased), Cardio 2×/week (engaging, low‑impact), Recovery/mobility daily short routines + 1–2 longer recovery sessions/week.
- Phases:
  - Phase 1 (Weeks 1–3): Base strength, motor control, glute/hip dominance, safe quad loading.
  - Week 4: Transition & increased volume.
  - Phase 2 Accumulation (Weeks 5–7): Increased volume and frequency (add 4th strength day), more unilateral and eccentric control.
  - Week 8: Active recovery (reduced intensity, technique focus).
  - Phase 3 Build/Peak (Weeks 9–10): Raise intensity; low-moderate volume (heavy singles/doubles/triples).
  - Week 11: Taper start (volume cut, quality maintained).
  - Week 12: Final taper/peak — arrive feeling strong, fresh, ski-ready.
- Nutrition: Aim for maintenance calories (start estimate ~30–35 kcal/kg). Protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg (target ~1.8 g/kg), fats 25–35% calories, carbs fill remainder. Creatine 3–5 g/day, omega‑3s, vitamin D; add 10–15 g collagen + vitamin C if desired.
- Recovery & Mobility: Daily 5–15 min maintenance, pre/post session and 1–2 weekly recovery sessions (pool option if knee irritated). Sleep 7–9 hours; monitor knee pain and swelling.

Assessment & baseline (before starting)
- Movement screen: single‑leg balance, step‑down control to ~60°, single‑leg RDL quality. Record comfortable working loads (RPE 6–7) and any ROM limits.
- Determine a conservative working “top set” for main lifts (use RPE and recent bests rather than true 1RMs unless tested safely).

Session templates (use each time)
- Warm-up (8–12 min): 5–8 min easy bike/elliptical + dynamic mobility (leg swings, thoracic rotations) + activation (band lateral walks, glute bridges, 1–2 light ramp sets).
- Main strength block: exercises & sets listed below per day.
- Accessory/core + finisher (8–12 min): posterior chain, single‑leg stability, core.
- Cool-down (5–10 min): foam roll, quad/hip flexor/hamstring stretches, breathing.
- Mobility/Recovery: daily 5–15 min routine (see details) and 1–2 weekly recovery sessions.

Progression rules & safety
- Increase load when all sets/reps completed with good form at RPE ≤7 and knee symptoms unchanged for 48 hours. Typical increases 2.5–5% or +2.5–5 lb on upper, 5–10 lb on lower lifts.
- Emphasize tempo on single‑leg/eccentric work (3–4 sec eccentrics).
- Avoid deep knee flexion under load and jumping; prefer box/partial squats, leg press limited ROM, and hip‑dominant lifts.
- If pain increases >2/10 or swelling appears: switch to pool/bike, reduce volume 30–50%, and consult clinician.

Full 12‑week week‑by‑week plan (concise but complete)

Weeks 1–3 — Phase 1: Base strength, control, glute dominance
Frequency: Strength 3×/week (Mon/Wed/Fri), Cardio 2×/week (Tue/Sat — one interval, one steady), Daily mobility.

Day A (Lower — Posterior focus + safe squats)
- RDL: 3 × 6–8
- Box squat (box approx. seat height to keep ≤60°): 3 × 6 (slow)
- Seated leg press (limited travel): 3 × 8–10
- Single‑leg RDL (DB): 3 × 8 each
- Standing calf raise: 3 × 12–15
- Pallof press: 3 × 10–12 each side
- Glute bridge / hip thrust (double‑leg): 3 × 8–12

Day B (Unilateral & stability)
- Bulgarian split (shallow): 3 × 6–8 each
- Goblet partial squat to box: 3 × 8–10
- Banded lateral walks: 3 × 12 steps each way
- Machine hamstring curl / single‑leg cable RDL: 3 × 8–10
- Single‑leg balance with reach: 3 × 30–40s each
- Dead bug: 3 × 8–10 each side

Day C (Upper + posterior chain stability)
- Bench or incline press: 4 × 6–8
- Chest‑supported row / bent‑over row: 4 × 6–8
- Landmine single‑arm press or DB strict press: 3 × 8
- Low box step‑ups (controlled, low height): 3 × 8 each
- Back extension / reverse hyper: 3 × 10–12
- Side plank: 3 × 30–45s each side

Cardio (2×/week)
- Interval (Session A): Pyramid 1–2–3–4–3–2–1 min hard/rest equal. Total 25–30 min.
- Steady (Session B): 20–30 min easy/moderate on bike/elliptical.

Mobility (daily)
- Mini morning flow (5–10 min): glute bridges 2×12, clamshells 2×12, quad isometrics 2×8, thoracic rotations 2×8.

Week 4 — Transition & increased volume
- Strength 3×/week + Cardio 2×/week.
- Add 1 set to main lifts, add conditioning finisher after one lower session (6 min bike + short bursts).
- Keep tempo and careful knee load control.

Weeks 5–7 — Phase 2: Accumulation (increase volume & frequency)
Frequency: Strength 4×/week (Mon/Tue/Thu/Fri), Cardio 2×/week (Wed/Sat). Active recovery modalities on rest days.

Sample week (Weeks 5–7)

Day 1 — Lower (Heavy hip dominant)
- Barbell RDL: 5 × 5
- Box squat (same box): 5 × 5
- Bulgarian split: 4 × 6–8 each
- Single‑leg RDL tempo: 4 × 6–8 each (4s ecc)
- Standing calf raise: 4 × 12
- Pallof: 3 × 12

Day 2 — Upper Heavy
- Bench press: 5 × 5
- Bent‑over or single‑arm row: 4–5 × 6–8
- Overhead press: 4 × 6–8
- Incline DB press: 3 × 8
- Pull‑up/pulldown: 3 × 6–8
- Farmer carry: 4 × 40–50 m

Day 3 — Cardio A (challenging)
- 30–35 min challenging interval (30/30 sprints or pyramid) or Mixed‑modal circuits (ski‑erg + bike + row).

Day 4 — Lower (Unilateral & eccentric)
- Trap/bar deadlift: 5 × 4–6
- Goblet partial squat slow ecc: 4 × 8
- Reverse lunge: 4 × 8 each (slow)
- Swiss‑ball hamstring curl: 4 × 8–12
- Single‑leg balance + perturbation: 4 × 30s

Day 5 — Upper/hybrid (added volume)
- Incline or close‑grip bench: 4 × 6
- Single‑arm row: 4 × 8 each
- Landmine press: 3 × 8 each
- Lat machine/high row: 3 × 10
- Arm superset: 3 × 10 each
- 10 min low‑impact bike finisher

Day 6 — Cardio B (longer steady)
- 35–45 min bike/elliptical; or pool session if knee feels sore.

Day 7 — Rest/mobility (longer recovery session 30–40 min as needed)

Progression notes for Weeks 5–7
- Increase load or sets only if all reps done with RPE ≤7 and no knee issues.
- Add small extra carbs on heavy days to maintain energy and weight.
- Use pool sessions if knee inflames.

Week 8 — Active recovery week
- Frequency: Strength 3×/week + Cardio 2×/week (lower intensity).
- Reduce intensity to ~70–80% of previous weeks; maintain 3–4 sets but lighter load; focus on tempo, clean technique and mobility.

Weeks 9–10 — Phase 3 Build & Peak (raise intensity; lower volume)
Goal: drive neural strength by increasing loads, decreasing volume.

Week 9 — Heavy intensity, moderate volume
- Strength 3–4×/week; Cardio 1–2×/week (lower volume).
- Main ideas:
  - Deadlifts/trap‑bar: 4 × 3–5 (work to RPE 8–9)
  - Box squat: 4 × 4–5 (heavy but controlled)
  - Hip thrust: 4 × 5–6 (heavier)
  - Keep single‑leg work moderate (3 sets), focus on control.

Week 10 — Peak intensity (highest loads, low volume)
- Strength 3×/week; Cardio minimal (one short interval).
- Main lifts: singles/doubles/triples
  - Deadlift/trap‑bar: 5–6 × 1–3 (work up to heavy singles/doubles at ~90–95% recent top; stop before grind)
  - Box squat: 4 × 2–3 (heavy)
  - Hip thrust: 3 × 3–5
  - Upper: bench 4–6 × 1–3
- Keep accessory volume minimal and focus on technique and CNS readiness.

Week 11 — Taper start
- Cut volume by ~40–50%, keep 1–2 heavy-ish exposures early in week.
- Lower sessions: 3 sets per movement at moderate loads; light single‑leg work.
- Cardio: 1 light steady or pool session.

Week 12 — Final taper & peak (feel strong & fresh)
- Low volume, low‑moderate intensity; 1–2 short quality sessions early in the week only.
- Example:
  - Early‑week: 2–3 × 1–2 reps at ~85–90% for trap‑bar/deadlift, then stop.
  - Mid‑week: light activation, tempo RDLs (2 × 4–5), partial squats 2 × 6 (fast concentric).
  - Avoid heavy lower hits within 48–72 hours of ski/testing.
- Cardio: 1 easy 20–30 min session; no hard intervals in final 72 hours.

Cardio — Twice weekly integrated plan (more engaging, progressive)
- Two sessions per week throughout, progressed across phases:
  - Session A (interval/challenging): rotate between Pyramid Intervals, 30/30 sprints, EMOM mixed row/ski, Hill intervals, Mixed‑modal circuits. Week 1–3 shorter; Weeks 5–7 increase rounds/duration; Weeks 9–10 shorten and keep low volume around heavy lifts; Week 12 light easy session.
  - Session B (steady/long): elliptical/bike/pool 20–60 min depending on phase (steady increases in Weeks 5–7; taper down Weeks 11–12).
- Use RPE and knee symptom checks. If knee inflames, swap to pool or reduce intensity.

Nutrition — Maintain weight while supporting strength
- Start estimate: ~30–35 kcal/kg (adjust with real weight). Example 82 kg → ~2,460–2,870 kcal/day; choose starting target ~2,700 kcal and adjust ±200 after 2 weeks based on weight trend.
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day. Target ~1.8 g/kg (e.g., 150 g/day for 82 kg).
- Fat: 25–35% of calories (~70–100 g/day depending on calories).
- Carbs: fill remaining calories to support training (higher on heavy/high-volume days).
- Supplements: creatine 3–5 g/day, fish oil 1–2 g EPA/DHA, vitamin D if needed, collagen 10–15 g + 50–100 mg vitamin C post‑session optional.
- Meal timing: distribute protein across 3–5 meals; carbs around workouts (30–60g pre/post as needed).
- Weigh weekly; adjust calories ±200 kcal if weight drifts >0.5–1.0 kg over two weeks.

Recovery & Mobility (daily + weekly)
- Daily maintenance (5–15 min): quad isometrics, glute bridges, clamshells, single‑leg balance, thoracic rotations.
- Pre‑session warm-up (8–12 min): bike/elliptical 5–8 min + dynamic mobility + band activation + 1–2 light ramp sets.
- Post‑session (8–12 min): foam rolling (quads/glutes/calves), hamstring/quad/hip flexor stretches, diaphragmatic breathing.
- 1–2 longer recovery sessions/week (30–50 min): pool/aqua sessions or mobility flow with soft tissue work.
- Knee‑specific drills: TKE band, partial step‑downs, terminal knee extension band, heel slides; progress depth gradually to ~60° only if pain free.
- Use ice for acute swelling after heavy sessions (10–15 min), and compression garments if helpful.
- Sleep 7–9 hours; hydration 2.5–3.5 L/day; prioritize anti‑inflammatory foods.

Peaking & testing guidance
- Weeks 9–10: heavy single/double/triple exposures. Stop heavy lifts if form breaks or knee pain arises.
- Week 11: start taper (cut volume).
- Week 12: arrive fresh — 1–2 short quality lifts early in week only. Avoid heavy lower work within 48–72 hours before skiing or testing.
- Ski readiness checklist: pain‑free single‑leg RDL and step‑downs to ~60° for 3×6–8, no persistent swelling after heavy sessions, ability to do 45–60 min low‑impact cardio without knee flare, physio/surgeon clearance for slope.

Monitoring & red flags
- Track knee pain 0–10 before/during/after sessions. If pain increases >2 points or swelling appears, reduce volume/load, switch to pool, and contact clinician.
- Watch movement compensations (knee valgus, trunk lean); address with extra unilateral and core work.
- Track weekly weight and training loads.
